input.quote: Section 7.1 No Resignation. The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated (Section 8.3), a multi-year term. Our only exit is cause-based: the Servicer may be removed under Section 7.2(c) solely if a Servicer Termination Event occurs and is continuing, and there is no at-will or convenience termination right anywhere for the Issuer or Depositor. The Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption mechanics in Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are Class A Certificateholder options subject to threshold, date and pricing conditions, not a Customer convenience right. That is the walk-away case of no Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months, so the fallback is not met on its material terms. The Vendor side is already better than both levels: Section 7.1 bars the Servicer from resigning except on legal inability, so the preferred no-Vendor-convenience element is already met and we do not touch it (adopting the fallback would actually give the Servicer an end-of-term convenience right it does not have today). We therefore target preferred and add only the missing Customer convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro rata refund of prepaid Servicing Fees; the new termination feeds the existing Successor Servicer machinery in Section 7.4, which triggers whenever the Servicer "is terminated under this Agreement". Servicing Fees are payable in arrears on each Payment Date, so the refund limb is protective only.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Add an Issuer right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro rata refund of prepaid Servicing Fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have no right to exit this servicing arrangement other than for a Servicer Termination Event, so we add a convenience termination right on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro rata refund of any prepaid Servicing Fees. Section 7.1 already prevents the Servicer from walking away mid-term, so no change is needed there; we can discuss a longer notice period if that is easier.

ops.text: Termination for Convenience. The Issuer may terminate this Agreement, and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement, for convenience and without cause, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, and the Servicer will refund, pro rata, any Servicing Fees paid in advance for any period after the effective date of the termination.
